action_trace.summary: Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (workflow enablement, abstract class design), pain points (groups parameter absence, pipeline failures), and acceptance criteria (stratified handling, reproducibility) for sklearn Issue #21356 SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement.

Questions target the SequentialFeatureSelector enhancement (Issue #21356) and abstract class design pattern, grounded in ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 requirements elicitation practices.

Generated 10 interview questions using 5W1H and Socratic techniques to elicit user goals (workflow enablement, abstract class rationale), pain points (current grouping limitations, validation failures), and acceptance criteria (edge cases, sklearn compatibility, prioritization). Questions decompose the SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter requirement into testable dimensions spanning user personas, failure scenarios, and design trade-offs aligned with ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 requirements elicitation practices.

End user requires SequentialFeatureSelector with groups parameter support to enable grouped feature selection in production ML workflows, addressing pain points around manual selection effort and feature dependency management while maintaining sklearn API consistency.

End-user requirements center on automating feature selection while respecting domain-specific feature groupings and providing transparent, justifiable selection rationale for business stakeholders. Abstract class interface with grouped selection support addresses manual selection bottlenecks and enables reproducible, interpretable feature engineering across diverse high-dimensional business domains.

End-user requirements focus on automating feature selection with domain-aware grouping constraints and standardized abstract interfaces to reduce manual engineering overhead, improve decision transparency, and enable strategy interchangeability in production ML pipelines.

Clarification needed on groups parameter semantics (strict vs partial selection), abstract class extension points for custom selection logic, tie-breaking strategies, ranking normalization across groups, error handling for missing features, reproducibility requirements, group size constraints, Pipeline integration scope, and support for hierarchical grouping to resolve ambiguities in the SequentialFeatureSelector design.

End-user raises 6 clarification questions addressing ambiguities in SequentialFeatureSelector's groups parameter semantics, abstract class tie-breaking behavior, extension mechanisms for non-greedy selection strategies, CV interaction, transparency requirements, and dependency constraint modeling to resolve conflicts between atomic grouping, strategy flexibility, and stakeholder justification needs.

Six clarification questions raised addressing ambiguities in SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter semantics (atomic vs. partial selection), tie-breaking determinism across implementations, abstract class extension scope (greedy vs. alternative criteria), interaction with scikit-learn ecosystem patterns, group-target conflicts, and transparency/explainability requirements for stakeholder justification.

End-user requirements validated: SequentialFeatureSelector with atomic group selection, deterministic tie-breaking, and extensible abstract class interface for forward/backward strategies. Refinements needed on soft vs. strict group constraints and optional custom selection criteria support.

End-user confirms atomic group selection requirement and refines tie-breaking mechanism (insertion order → alphabetical → strategy-specific) for SequentialFeatureSelector. Abstract class interface validated with mandatory extension points (evaluation criterion, selection strategy, stopping condition) and optional support for alternative selection criteria. Requirements address pain points (manual bottlenecks, transparency) and enable domain-aware feature selection with reproducible behavior.

End-user requirements validated and refined: SequentialFeatureSelector must support atomic group selection via fit(groups) parameter with deterministic tie-breaking (insertion order → alphabetical → strategy-specific); abstract class interface standardizes forward/backward selection with mandatory extension points (evaluation criterion, selection strategy, stopping condition) and optional support for alternative criteria, enabling automated domain-aware feature selection and consistent strategy-swapping without pipeline restructuring.

Consolidated 7 structured elicitation records from EndUser dialogue (sklearn SequentialFeatureSelector Issue #21356) addressing: (1) atomic group selection via fit() groups parameter to preserve feature dependencies, (2) standardized abstract class interface with mandatory extension points for consistent forward/backward selection behavior, (3) deterministic tie-breaking mechanism prioritizing insertion order then alphabetical ordering, (4) optional support for alternative selection criteria beyond greedy approaches, (5) transparent ranking mechanisms for stakeholder justification. All records ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 compliant with priority levels (MUST/SHOULD/COULD) and traceability to source confirmations.

Seven prioritized user requirements synthesized from 6 interview records and enduser confirmations: 2 MUST (atomic group selection enforcement, standardized abstract class interface with 3 mandatory extension points), 3 SHOULD (deterministic tie-breaking, optional extension points for alternative criteria, strategy-swappable pipeline design), 1 COULD (transparent ranking/justification), 1 WON'T (deferred non-deterministic criteria). All requirements traced to specific interview statements and enduser validations per ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 traceability requirements.

Formulated seven targeted questions probing infrastructure constraints (deployment environments, serialization), scalability expectations (10k+ feature handling, deterministic ordering performance), security mandates (reproducibility, audit trails), backwards compatibility, pipeline integration, observability requirements, and failure mode handling to ground abstract class design decisions in operational realities.

Formulated 8 targeted questions probing infrastructure constraints (deployment environments, resource limits, compatibility), security mandates (audit trails, data governance, feature provenance), scalability expectations (dimensionality handling, parallelization), extension point readiness, performance thresholds, monitoring requirements, and integration dependencies. Questions grounded in MoSCoW priorities (M-001 through M-003, S-001 through S-002, C-001) and designed to elicit deployer constraints that shape abstract class design decisions, tie-breaking implementation, and optional extension mechanisms.

Eight targeted questions probe deployer constraints across infrastructure scalability, security/compliance mandates, backward compatibility, extension governance, audit/reproducibility requirements, pipeline integration patterns, and resource constraints—enabling validation that the abstract class interface for SequentialFeatureSelector with atomic groups parameter is deployable, maintainable, and operationally sound.

Deployer confirms infrastructure readiness: SequentialFeatureSelector groups parameter and abstract class interface deploy on existing scikit-learn CI/CD with no new infrastructure; scalability targets 10K features/1K groups within 2GB memory; security enforced via groups immutability and atomic validation; tie-breaking follows deterministic insertion-order-then-alphabetical ordering; backward compatibility maintained via optional groups parameter; zero additional operational cost.

Deployer response addresses infrastructure deployment on scikit-learn CI/CD (Python 3.8+), scalability targets (10K features, 2GB memory), security mandates (immutable groups, input validation), deterministic tie-breaking procedures (insertion-order, alphabetical), cost optimization via existing resources, and availability/performance trade-offs for atomic group selection enforcement.

Deploy SequentialFeatureSelector abstract class with atomic groups parameter on scikit-learn's GitHub Actions CI/CD (Python 3.8+) supporting 10,000 features/1,000 groups within 2GB memory using O(1) lazy tie-breaking; enforce groups immutability and validation at fit() entry; implement deterministic tie-breaking (insertion order→alphabetical→strategy-specific); reuse existing infrastructure to minimize cost while maintaining reproducibility and backward compatibility.

Deployer role identified six operational context gaps requiring clarification: memory profiling strategy (peak vs. steady-state), immutability scope across fit() calls, test fixture requirements for extension points, group validation constraints comprehensiveness, tie-breaking insertion order semantics, and infrastructure dependency management. These gaps must be resolved to ensure deployment feasibility and security/scalability mandate satisfaction.

Deployer requires six operational clarifications on memory profiling scope, immutability lifecycle, extension point testing strategy, lazy evaluation timing, group validation rules, and cost-performance trade-off priorities to resolve infrastructure constraints and security mandate ambiguities before SequentialFeatureSelector abstract class deployment.

SRS violates ISO/IEC/IEEE 29148 quality attributes across 10 critical findings: clarity defects in template-derived boilerplate and informal language; verifiability gaps in tie-breaking acceptance criteria and extension point contracts; feasibility conflicts between 2GB memory envelope and lazy evaluation mandate; consistency contradictions in immutability lifecycle scope and stopping condition specification; traceability absence in GitHub issue cross-referencing; redundancy in IR-to-requirement duplication. Recommend: (1) Replace informal fragments with structured requirement templates, (2) Define BaseSequentialSelector method signatures with parametric constraints, (3) Add measurable verification conditions for tie-breaking and memory profiling, (4) Clarify immutability scope in SRS-2.1, (5) Consolidate IR/user requirement/system requirement traceability chain, (6) Specify artifact generation strategy for transparency feature.

All six review findings (clarity, verifiability, feasibility, consistency, traceability violations) resolved through SRS revisions and knowledge artifact alignment. Atomic groups enforcement, deterministic tie-breaking, abstract class extension points, and memory scalability constraints now formally specified with acceptance criteria and design bindings. Closure confirmed for sklearn_2021q4 SequentialFeatureSelector feature selection enhancement.
